claims.claim: Screen flow is an explicit finite-state enum: Splash → Unlock/Create → Init → Main, matching the module doc-comment.
enum Screen defines the five top-level screens (Splash, Unlock, Create, Init, Main) that gate both rendering (ui.rs render()) and key dispatch (handle_key).
Within Screen::Main, a Mode enum (Browsing, AddContact, InRoom) further gates keybinding dispatch inside handle_main_key.

Keyboard input is read on a dedicated OS thread (blocking crossterm::event::read(), filtered to KeyEventKind::Press) and forwarded to the async event loop via an unbounded mpsc channel, rather than being polled inside tokio::select! directly.
The main event loop is a single tokio::select! over four sources: the keyboard channel, the session-event channel, the Tor-bootstrap channel, and a 100ms tick interval.

Starting a session (Enter on a selected contact) aborts any previous conn_task, opens fresh SessionCmd/SessionEvent channels, and spawns a tokio task that calls transport::establish(...) then session::run_session(conn, role, local_sk, Some(peer_pk), o_rx, e_tx).

RoomState enum (None, Connecting, Handshaking, Open, PeerLeft, Closed) tracks connection lifecycle and is transitioned exclusively via handle_session_event reacting to SessionEvent::StateChanged/PeerLeft/Error/Notice.

leave_room aborts the background connection task, drops the SessionCmd/SessionEvent channels, and clears the in-memory message list, explicitly noting to the user 'Riwayat dibuang' (history discarded).

Chat messages exist only in App.messages: Vec<ChatLine> for the lifetime of a room; there is no on-disk persistence of chat history in this file — messages.clear() runs both when a new room starts and when a room is left.
claims.notes: messages.clear() also called at line 895 (start_connection) and 1009 (leave_room).

claims.claim: try_unlock reads vault bytes from disk then calls vault::unseal with the raw passphrase bytes; on failure it distinguishes an unreadable vault file ('Vault tidak terbaca.') from a failed unseal ('Passphrase salah atau vault rusak.') but the unseal-failure message does not itself distinguish wrong-passphrase from corrupted-ciphertext.
claims.notes: Underlying vault::unseal algorithm was not read in this task (identity/vault.rs out of scope), so whether this message discipline is deliberate anti-oracle design cannot be confirmed here.

claims.claim: create_vault generates a brand-new KeyBundle::generate(), seals it via vault::seal with the entered passphrase, and writes the sealed bytes to app.vault_path; the UI requires the passphrase to be entered twice and compares them with a plain String != check before proceeding.
claims.notes: Confirmation compare is at line 522 (app.pass_confirm != app.pass_input) inside handle_create_key (497-546); this is a local same-process UX check, not a remote-auth comparison.

claims.claim: Passphrase input is accumulated in plain String fields (pass_input, pass_confirm), pushed one char at a time, and reset via .clear() after use in several branches; String::clear() truncates length without guaranteeing the freed heap bytes are zeroed, and no Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop wrapper is applied to these fields in this file.
claims.notes: .clear() call sites: 482, 487, 524-525, 530-531. This is a factual API-behavior observation, not a claim of exploitability.

claims.claim: SelfKeys.noise_sk: [u8; 32] (the Noise/X25519 static secret) is stored as a plain byte array on App.keys with no visible Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop in this file, and the same static secret is read fresh from app.keys and reused for every new connection attempt.
claims.notes: Reuse point: start_connection line 908 (let local_sk = keys.noise_sk;). Whether the underlying vault/keypair modules apply zeroization elsewhere cannot be confirmed from this file.

claims.claim: Contact fingerprint is computed by contacts::fingerprint(ed25519_pub, noise_pub), binding both the Ed25519 identity key and the X25519 Noise key into one displayed string; a code comment states this fingerprint 'HARUS' bind both keys because it is what the user manually verifies out-of-band.
claims.notes: Same call pattern also at mod.rs:907 and ui.rs:495-497 (comment) /497 (call). Fingerprint hash algorithm itself is not visible in these two files.

claims.claim: The contacts file path is derived deterministically from the vault file's stem plus a '-contacts' suffix and stored in the same directory as the vault.

A 32-byte contacts_key is derived once at unlock/create time via contacts::derive_contacts_key(&bundle) and passed to contacts::load_contacts/save_contacts as the key argument for the on-disk contacts store.
claims.notes: Derivation call sites: 569, 587. Whether/how the store is encrypted with this key is implemented in the contacts module, not visible in tui/mod.rs.

claims.claim: On unlock, contacts loaded from disk are merged with any contacts passed in at startup, de-duplicated by ed25519_pub equality (startup contacts inserted at front only if not already present), then immediately re-persisted to disk.

persist_contacts failure only raises a non-blocking warning notification ('Peringatan: gagal menyimpan kontak ke disk.'); there is no retry and the in-memory contact list is not rolled back, so UI state and disk state can silently diverge.
load_contacts_into silently ignores a failed contacts::load_contacts call via an `if let Ok(disk) = ...` pattern, falling back to only the startup-supplied contacts with no user-facing error message.

Global Ctrl+C is checked first in handle_key (before any screen-specific dispatch) and immediately terminates the TUI loop from any screen without explicitly aborting an in-flight app.conn_task or notifying the peer session; the same unconditional-quit pattern applies to Esc on Splash/Unlock/Create/Init and to q/Esc while browsing contacts.
claims.notes: Additional Esc-quit sites: 479 (Unlock), 499 (Create), 550 (Init), 655 (Browsing q/Esc). Actual task cleanup on process exit depends on tokio runtime shutdown behavior not visible in this file.

claims.claim: handle_session_event treats SessionEvent::Notice as non-fatal (only shows a warning + system chat line, room state untouched, per an explicit code comment) while SessionEvent::Error forces RoomState::Closed and shows an error notification plus a system chat line.

There is no file or structured logging in this module; user-visible status is only an ephemeral in-memory Notification (levels Error/Warn/Success/Info). Success notices auto-dismiss after 30 ticks (~3s at 100ms/tick) and Info after 40 ticks (~4s), while Error/Warn persist until replaced.
The terminal must be at least 80x24 characters (MIN_WIDTH/MIN_HEIGHT); below that, render() replaces the entire screen with a size-warning card via render_too_small instead of any interactive UI.

Chat scrolling and 'Mode Light' recency dimming (last BLUR_KEEP_RECENT=3 messages stay unblurred) both depend on estimate_wrapped_lines, which the code's own 'ponytail' comment documents as a char-count/effective-width approximation of ratatui's real word-boundary wrap, not an exact replication — long-word-heavy text can make the scroll/dim estimate diverge from actual rendered line counts.
claims.notes: BLUR_KEEP_RECENT defined at mod.rs:212; used at ui.rs:583 and 609.

claims.claim: 'Mode Light' can be scoped locally ([L], nothing sent to peer) or synced ([B], sends SessionCmd::Blur(true) to the peer session) via a modal prompt; toggling off only re-sends SessionCmd::Blur(false) if the mode had previously been synced.

Reply quoting clips the quoted text to QUOTE_MAX=40 characters with a trailing ellipsis before prefixing it to the outgoing message text via format_reply; the composite text is what actually gets sent as SessionCmd::Text.
claims.notes: Send path: send_message, lines 976-993, SessionCmd::Text at line 988.

claims.claim: Message search (Ctrl+S) is a case-insensitive substring match over each message's text using to_lowercase().contains(...), recomputed on every keystroke; an empty query yields zero matches by design.

The invite-code popup splits the invite string into fixed 44-byte chunks of its raw bytes for display (invite.as_bytes().chunks(44)) and decodes each chunk with str::from_utf8(..).unwrap_or("") — a chunk boundary that split a multi-byte UTF-8 codepoint would silently render as empty text for that chunk; this only affects the on-screen popup, since copy_invite's clipboard path copies the original, unchunked String.

ChatLine.time is stamped with chrono::Local::now() at the moment a message is pushed into the local `messages` Vec (for both own and peer messages); the struct's own doc comment explicitly notes this is local UI time, not a timestamp carried over the wire/protocol.

Test blur_prompt_local_activates_without_sending verifies that pressing 'l' in the Mode Light prompt enables blur locally, leaves blur_synced false, closes the prompt, and sends nothing on the SessionCmd channel.
Test blur_prompt_both_sends_command verifies that pressing 'b' in the Mode Light prompt enables blur, sets blur_synced true, and sends SessionCmd::Blur(true) on the channel.
Test blur_prompt_esc_cancels verifies that pressing Esc while the Mode Light prompt is open closes the prompt without enabling blur.
Test toggle_blur_off_sends_command_when_synced verifies that toggling off an active+synced Mode Light disables both flags and sends SessionCmd::Blur(false).
Test format_reply_clips_long_quote verifies a 50-character quote is truncated with an ellipsis while the reply body still appears intact after it.
Test format_reply_keeps_short_quote_intact verifies a short quote ('halo') is not truncated or ellipsized.
Test search_messages_case_insensitive verifies substring search matches regardless of case ('dunia' matches 'Halo Dunia') and that empty or no-match queries return an empty result vector.
Test estimate_wrapped_lines_short_text_is_one_line verifies that short text ('halo') at width 80 estimates to exactly 1 line.

Test estimate_wrapped_lines_long_text_spans_multiple_lines verifies that a 200-character string at width 80 (effective width 76 after the 4-char prefix allowance) estimates to 3 lines, documenting the ceil(len/effective_width) formula.

Test estimate_wrapped_lines_zero_width_does_not_panic verifies the estimator does not panic/divide-by-zero when width is 0 (falls back to an effective width of 1 via .max(1)), returning 4 for a 4-character string.

The #[cfg(test)] modules in both files cover only pure logic helpers (Mode Light toggle/prompt, reply formatting, message search, wrap-line estimation); no test in these two files exercises vault unlock/create, contact add/delete/persist-to-disk, or the network session-establishment path (start_connection, handle_session_event) — those are only reachable through manual or integration-level exercising outside these files.
claims.notes: Based on absence within the two test modules read (mod.rs:1061-1147, ui.rs:994-1014); other test files elsewhere in the crate were not reviewed in this task.
